acceptance.check: On the Schedules page, a schedule set to repeat monthly for 1 occurrence opens a context menu that does NOT contain 'Skip next scheduled date', while a never-ending monthly schedule's menu still does.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA can build this by hand: Add new schedule, leave Repeats checked, click the recurrence description button to open the picker, set the end dropdown to 'for' (occurrences = 1), Apply, Add. The exhausted row must show Post transaction / Post transaction today / Complete / Delete and no Skip item. The browser-verifiable form of the regression: if the four skip call sites were reverted to scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond), this row would wrongly gain a Skip item. The automated guard is the e2e case named in tests[].

acceptance.check: Double-clicking the body of a Schedules row opens exactly one schedule edit modal, and pressing Cancel once returns to the Schedules list.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Create any schedule so a row exists, double-click the row body (the payee cell, not the actions dots), observe a single 'Schedule name' field, press Cancel once, observe the Schedules table with no modal remaining. Before this change two stacked modals appear and Cancel dismisses only the top one.

acceptance.check: Opening a schedule for editing and pressing Cancel produces no React 'value prop on an input should not be null' or 'changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled' warning in the browser console.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Save a schedule with no name (leave Schedule name blank on the Add form), then open it for editing from the Schedules row. Filter the console for 'uncontrolled' and 'null'; observe nothing. The automated guard is the e2e case named in tests[] — no browser sees a dev-mode console warning the way the Playwright collector does.

acceptance.check: The e2e console guard is narrowed to the product: it collects only React's two input warnings, and the file no longer contains the probe constants or the self-check loop that proved the regex matches strings held in the same file.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Read packages/desktop-client/e2e/schedules.test.ts. REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, the reactInputWarning.source.split('|') loop, and the page.evaluate that console.errors the literals must all be absent; reactInputWarning, CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, watchReactInputWarnings, the waitForTimeout drain and expect(messages).toEqual([]) must all be present. Not browser-observable — it is a property of the test file's contents.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA's double-click by teaching pushModal to ignore a push identical to the top of the stack — the guard the ticket's suspected-cause paragraph points at.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: 231 call sites depend on pushModal's unconditional append, and modal options carry callbacks (onClose, onSave, onScheduleLinked at modalsSlice.ts:112/167/341) that no equality check can compare, so 'identical' is not decidable at that layer. The narrower replaceModal at the one call site QA reported fixes the reported defect at a fraction of the blast radius, and the codebase already uses replaceModal this way at Sidebar.tsx:31 and AccountsPage.tsx:565.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA's double-click by debouncing the Row's onClick in SchedulesTable.tsx, or by ignoring a click whose MouseEvent detail is 2.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Timing-based, and `detail === 2` drops the second click without knowing whether the first already opened the modal — it makes the symptom rarer rather than the behaviour correct, and pushes the rule into a shared table component for one page's sake.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take the second menu-scoping finding at face value and leave getByRole('menu') unscoped, matching the six other uses in the suite.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The consistency argument is a style argument and it loses to a correctness one: the added expect(menu).toBeVisible() is Playwright's strict mode and throws on a multi-match, while the two consumers that read the menu tolerate any number of matches. `.last()` is correct because the context menu renders in a portal opened last, and scoping one locator cannot affect the six sites this change does not touch. This is the one place two findings on this ticket pointed opposite ways, so I state the call rather than splitting the difference.

alternatives_considered.approach: Build the exhausted-recurrence fixture by typing 1 into `#end_occurrences`, as the finding's recipe says.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The field is uncontrolled and already seeded to the number 1 (useScheduleEdit.ts:201, RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:454). Typing delivers the string '1' through onChangeValue into `config.endOccurrences`, which recurConfigToRSchedule copies verbatim into rrule's `count` (schedules.ts:287) and getRecurringDescription compares to 1 strictly (schedule.ts:59) — so the write introduces a string where the code expects a number, for no gain. The fixture is correct the moment endMode switches; asserting the field reads '1' is stronger than writing to it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give the exhausted-recurrence fixture a schedule name, and cover the edit path by opening a named schedule instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Then the edit path seeds `fields.name` to a string and never reaches the `?? null` branch at useScheduleEdit.ts:119 — which is the branch finding (C) is about. Leaving the name off makes one fixture cover both the skip divergence and the nullable-name edit path.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split the eight findings into separate tickets via a scope_changed route request, since the eight are not one change.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ticket was filed deliberately as one lot against one merged PR, all eight findings converge on the same two e2e files plus one two-line reducer swap, and the split candidate that could matter — QA's bug versus the e2e hygiene — is two lines against fifty and shares no file. Splitting would spend a maintainer round to separate work that reviews cleanly as one commit. Recorded here rather than requested so the reasoning is visible if a human disagrees.

validated_work_order.approach:
Four edits, in dependency order.

1. Make the exhausted recurrence reachable from a test. RecurringSchedulePicker already renders the recipe the review names — a Select at `id="repeat_end_dropdown"` whose 'for' option is the `after_n_occurrences` endMode, and an Input at `id="end_occurrences"` — but neither the picker trigger nor the ScheduleEditModal page model reaches them. Add `data-testid="recurrence-description"` to the picker's trigger Button (RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:629); its accessible name is prose regenerated from the config and cannot be a selector. Add `ScheduleEditModal.setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences(count)`: click the trigger, click `#repeat_end_dropdown`, click the 'for' option, then Apply. Do NOT type into `#end_occurrences` — it is uncontrolled, already seeded to the number 1, and typing pushes the string '1' through onChangeValue into `base.count`, while `getRecurringDescription` compares `endOccurrences === 1` strictly, so a string flips the label to the plural and puts a string in rrule's count. Assert `#end_occurrences` reads "1" instead of writing to it.

2. Add the exhausted fixture and assert the divergence. A monthly rule with count 1 and start = today has exactly one occurrence, which is its next_date. getNextDateAfter advances start until it finds an occurrence strictly greater than afterDate; with one occurrence it advances past it and returns null. scheduleIsSkippable is therefore false while scheduleIsRecurring is true — the one input where they differ, and the input no existing fixture produces. Build it with payee 'Lowes Hardware' (distinct from the test's 'Home Depot' and 'Apple'), no schedule name, so the same fixture also drives finding (C). Locate it by payee filter like the existing two rows; both are already located by payee rather than index, so adding a third row does not move the recurring assertion.

3. Exercise the edit path on that fixture. Leaving the name off is what makes finding (C) fixable in the same step: `fill()` skips scheduleName when absent, so the saved schedule has name null, and opening it for edit seeds `fields.name = schedule.name ?? null` — the branch the console guard exists to protect. Add `SchedulesPage.editSchedule(row)` that clicks the row's payee cell and returns a ScheduleEditModal, then open the exhausted schedule for editing and cancel it inside the watched window, before the drain and the assertion.

4. Delete the self-test. Remove REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES and its comment, the alternatives loop, and the trailing probe block, keeping reactInputWarning, CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, watchReactInputWarnings, the unconditional waitForTimeout drain and expect(messages).toEqual([]). That is the whole of the command-bar.test.ts:64-95 shape the original order asked for.

Separately, fix QA's bug at the schedules call site rather than in the shared reducer: switch onEdit from pushModal to replaceModal. There is precedent — Sidebar.tsx:31 and AccountsPage.tsx:565 both replaceModal for add-account — and it is safe here because the Schedules page's onEdit is reached only from that page; the other SchedulesTable consumer, ScheduleLink.tsx:143, passes its own onSelect that closes its own modal. Changing pushModal itself would touch 231 call sites and its options carry callbacks (onClose, onSave, onScheduleLinked) that no equality check can compare.

Finally the mechanical rename and the two findings resolved without code changes, both stated in the work order so review does not re-raise them.
assumptions: The Schedules page's onEdit is reached only from that page, so replaceModal flattening the stack cannot discard a modal a user still needs. Verified: the only other SchedulesTable consumer is ScheduleLink.tsx:143, which passes its own onSelect that closes its own modal.

The Playwright viewport for this suite is desktop-width, so RecurringSchedulePicker takes its Popover branch rather than the isNarrowWidth Modal branch. If a run is narrow, #repeat_end_dropdown and #end_occurrences still resolve — both are rendered by the same component either way — but the picker would live in a modal rather than a popover.

The demo budget's payees do not already contain 'Lowes Hardware' or 'Ace Hardware'. Both are new names introduced by this change; the suite's existing fixtures already create arbitrary payees the same way, so a collision would surface as a toHaveCount(1) failure rather than a silent pass.
The recurring-schedule prose on the picker trigger is locale-dependent, which is why the new locator keys on a data-testid rather than on the prose.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every line of code the plan names was read directly and matches: the four skip call sites, scheduleIsSkippable's two-clause body, setNextDate's silent drop, the unconditional append in pushModal and its keyboard-shortcuts exception, useScheduleEdit.ts:119's `?? null`, ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134's `|| ''` guard, the Select/Input/Menu markup behind each new selector, and the diff of PR #68 that produced the hoisted fixture. The arithmetic that makes the new fixture discriminating I traced by hand through getNextDateAfter and recurConfigToRSchedule. What holds confidence below 90: no Playwright browser is installed in this checkout, so no test in this plan was executed — the four interaction recipes (picker popover, dblclick coordinates, edit-then-cancel, console drain) are derived from source and are the part most likely to need a selector adjusted on the first run. QA's bug is confirmed by reading the full dispatch chain but not reproduced in a browser, which is why `reproduced` is false rather than true. The two findings I decline are declined on stated technical grounds, not preference, and I recorded the reasoning so a reviewer can overturn either call cheaply. Above the 70 gate because the shape of the change is unambiguous and the uncertainty is confined to selector spelling.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: Single-agent plan (config sets councils.plan: single), so no council debate to summarize. Three judgement calls were made explicitly rather than silently, and each is recorded where review would look for it. (1) Two findings on schedules-page.ts:115 gave opposite recommendations — scope getByRole('menu') or leave it for consistency. I scoped it with .last(): strict-mode toBeVisible() throws on multi-match while count()/allTextContents() tolerate many, and the context menu portals open last. (2) I dropped the weeklyOnSaturday revert, against the reviewer's own stated fix ("keep the annotation unless a caller needs it") — scheduleIsSkippable takes a union keyed on `field`, so the sibling describe cannot pass the fixture without both, and getNextDateAfter reads only .op/.value. (3) I fixed QA's double-click with replaceModal at the call site rather than the pushModal guard the ticket's suspected-cause paragraph points at, because 231 call sites share that reducer and modal options carry callbacks no equality check can compare. Also declined the review's instruction to type 1 into #end_occurrences: the field is uncontrolled and already seeded to the number 1, so typing puts a string into rrule's count for no gain.

getNextDateAfter (schedules.ts:393-411) advances start until it finds an occurrence strictly greater than afterDate, with MAX_ADVENCE_ATTEMPTS = 7; with a single occurrence it advances past it and returns null.

validated_work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes. The missing regression coverage exists because the e2e fixtures happen to sit outside the only input where scheduleIsSkippable and scheduleIsRecurring differ: a one-off's plain-date condition already fails scheduleIsRecurring (PR #59), and a never-ending monthly has a successor under both predicates. The unit tests call the predicate directly, so no call site is pinned. validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #74 bundles eight follow-ups left behind by PR #68 (issue #61): seven non-blocking review findings on the schedules e2e suite and its page models, plus one pre-existing QA bug about a double-clicked Schedules row stacking two edit modals. They are not one change and I treat them as four. (A) The ticket's one behavioural fix — hiding Skip on an exhausted recurrence — has no test that fails without it: the e2e fixtures build a one-off via uncheckRepeats (whose plain-date condition already made scheduleIsRecurring false, from PR #59) and a never-ending monthly (for which getNextDateAfter returns a date under both predicates), so neither fixture is the one input where scheduleIsSkippable and scheduleIsRecurring disagree. The loot-core unit tests call scheduleIsSkippable directly, so reverting all four call sites leaves the suite green. (B) The e2e console guard grew ~50 lines past what the work order asked for: REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, an alternatives-matching loop, and a page.evaluate that console.errors the two literals back into the page. All three prove the filter matches strings held as constants in the same file. (C) The AC-4 console guard only ever drives the add path, so the edit path's nullable name seed (useScheduleEdit.ts:119, `name: schedule.name ?? null`) is never exercised. (D) QA's double-click bug: SchedulesTable.tsx's Row onClick fires once per click, the Schedules page wires onSelect to onEdit, and onEdit dispatches pushModal, whose reducer (modalsSlice.ts:755-770) appends unconditionally apart from a keyboard-shortcuts special case — so the second click of a double-click pushes a second identical modal. I verified every line of that chain by reading the source; I did not make the failure happen in a browser (see confidence_rationale). Two findings are the same line with opposite recommendations and I resolve them explicitly below. One finding I drop as not holding up, also with reasons.
